newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt approves Germany reconciliation pact.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt approves Germany reconciliation pact.

text.p: The Czech government has approved the text of a long-awaited declaration on post-World War Two reconciliation with Germany, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Tuesday
Klaus said the government had given him the authority to sign the text, which is expected to be intitialled on Friday in Prague by foreign ministers of both countries.
The declaration must also be signed by the two countries' presidents and confirmed by the two parliaments.

"In this declaration it is clearly stated that the will of both sides is to close the past, to close the negative chapters of our history. This declaration means a clear turn in our relations toward the future," Klaus told a news conference
The document contains mutual expressions of regret for the Nazi occupation from 1938 to 1945 and for excessive brutality during the post-war expulsion of the Sudeten Germans.

The declaration also sets up a Czech-German Future Fund with the German side paying in 140 million marks ($90 million), and the Czechs paying about one-seventh of that to finance "projects of common interest". They include environmental, historical and scientific projects and youth meetings.
